Reproducing Saez and Friedlander (2016) from CRCNS pvc-9¶

Paper. Saez I, Friedlander MJ (2016). Role of GABAA-mediated inhibition and functional assortment of synapses onto individual layer 4 neurons in regulating plasticity expression in visual cortex. PLoS One 11(2): e0147642. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0147642. The claims file (claims/saez-2016.yaml) was written from the version of record (PMC4739708, open access): main text, Methods and the legends of Figures 1 to 3. The paper has no supplement and links no code.

Data set. CRCNS pvc-9, doi:10.6080/K00V89R6, streamed from the public S3 bucket (crcnsarchive/pvc-9/live/data.tar.gz, MD5 217a64766d19e7ad87efa4e339b82295 in the data set's checksums.md5). CRCNS data sets are not versioned (docs/archives.md), so the version is recorded as unversioned. This is the only published copy: the bucket holds one data file, under live/, and no old/ folder; the paper cites the data set's DOI and no version. The MD5 above lets a later change be seen.

What the data set holds. Whole-cell recordings (Axon ABF files, 20 kHz) of layer 4 cells in guinea pig V1 slices: extracellular stimulation at 0.2 Hz before and after a pairing protocol, in three folders, current clamp control (Data_ECS_IC), voltage clamp control (Data_ECS_VC) and voltage clamp with bicuculline (Data_ECS_VCB), one subfolder per recording. Three Excel files mark which recordings the paper included (green) and which it excluded (red), and hold the authors' own per-sweep amplitudes and per-cell changes. The single-cell stimulation (SCS) data of the paper's reference 17, which Figure 3 uses, are not in it.

Method. The claims file fixes the per-cell measure (peak amplitude of the evoked response less a 10 ms pre-stimulus baseline, searched from the end of the stimulus artifact to 50 ms), the pre-pairing epoch (120 sweeps), the classification (Student's t-test p < 0.05 and a change beyond 15%), and names the open details as readings: the post-pairing window (P) (a) all post-pairing sweeps, (b) the first 120, (c) the last 120; and the per-cell t-test (T) (a) on sweep amplitudes, (b) on 1-min bin means. Every reading is run. Details taken from the paper or chosen here are in pvc9.py and listed in the summary. No random numbers are used.

Revision after round 1 of verification. Each sweep is now aligned on the onset of the stimulus artifact (the first version used its largest step, which fell on either phase of the artifact from sweep to sweep), and sweeps without a stimulus artifact are dropped (four post-pairing sweeps of IC13, with spikes or no stimulus, had been measured as responses, and one VCB19 sweep pinned at the amplifier's limit). The data check adds VCB17's traces, IC13 against its sheet, the alignment and baseline variants, the fill of every Summary sheet row, and a per-cell table of the control cells.

import pvc9

      f"{len(members)} tar members, {len(files)} ABF files reduced, Excel files: {sorted(sheets)}")

The archive matches the descriptor's three folders, with 21 IC, 17 VC and 38 VCB recording folders. Besides ABF files it holds Clampfit .sta files, three .tmp files and one .bak file, which the descriptor does not mention and which are not used.

The descriptor gives 20 kHz and 500 ms sweeps "triggered once every 10 seconds". Most files are 20 kHz with 0.5 s sweeps, but the test sweeps are every 5 s (0.2 Hz), as the Methods state; the 10 s interval is that of the pairing files ("Extracellular pairing", 60 trials at 0.1 Hz, Methods). The descriptor's 10 s is wrong for the test sweeps (a finding). A few files are at 10 kHz with 1 s sweeps: they are the derived *_PRE/*_POST files, not used. Current clamp files are in mV and voltage clamp files in pA, except the pairing files, which are recorded in current clamp (mV), as the Methods describe.

The Summary sheets mark exactly the paper's 14 IC, 14 VC and 26 bicuculline recordings as included, and 9, 11 and 12 as excluded, the Methods' discard counts. The recordings themselves are incomplete for eight included control cells. IC22, IC23, VC21 and VC25 have no folder (the archive has folders IC1 to IC21 and VC1 to VC17, matching the descriptor's counts of 21 and 17, which are smaller than the sheets' 23 and 25). The folders VC10 and VC17 end with the pairing file and hold no post-pairing recording. The IC11 sheet names a one-sweep file as the pairing and the real pairing file (60 trials) as the post-pairing recording, so its post-pairing recording is not in the folder. The IC7 sheet names 07305017 as post-pairing; that file has no protocol name, no recording date, a 0.5 s sweep interval and no stimulus artifact near 108 ms (its largest step is at about 141 ms, against 107.9 ms in IC7's baseline file 07305013), so it is not a post-pairing test recording. The folder IC6 is empty, and its files (07305007 to 07305011, as the IC6 sheet lists them) are in the folder IC7; IC6 is analysed from them. So 10 of 14 IC, 10 of 14 VC and 26 of 26 bicuculline recordings are complete: 20 of the 28 control cells. All of this is a finding about the data.

# Files deposited more than once: the derived files (Concatenate*, *_PRE, *_POST) against the original
# recordings, by an MD5 of each sweep's samples.
orig = files[~pvc9.is_derived(files.file)]
by_md5 = {}
for i, r in orig.iterrows():
    for k, h in enumerate(r.sweep_md5):
        by_md5.setdefault(h, []).append((r.folder, r.file, k))
rows = []
for _, r in files[pvc9.is_derived(files.file)].iterrows():
    hits = [by_md5.get(h, []) for h in r.sweep_md5]
    src = sorted({f"{x[0]}/{x[1]}" for h in hits for x in h})
    rows.append(dict(folder=r.folder, file=r.file, sweeps=r.n_sweeps, units=r.units, rate=r.rate,
                     sweeps_found_in_originals=sum(bool(h) for h in hits), originals=" ".join(s.split("/")[1][:8] for s in src)))
dup = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(dup.to_string(index=False))
same = [(k, v) for k, v in by_md5.items() if len({(x[0], x[1]) for x in v}) > 1]
print("\nSweeps shared by two original recordings:", len(same))
for h, v in same:
    print("  ", v)
dr = files[pvc9.is_derived(files.file)]
print("Derived files whose header gives 10 kHz:", dr[dr.rate == 10000].file.tolist(), "; samples per sweep:",
      sorted({int(round(x)) for x in (dr[dr.rate == 10000].sweep_s * dr[dr.rate == 10000].rate)}),
      "; originals:", sorted({int(round(x)) for x in (orig[orig.rate == 20000].sweep_s * 20000) if x == 10000}))
for h, v in same:
    for folder, fname, k in v:
        r = files[(files.folder == folder) & (files.file == fname)].iloc[0]
        print(f"  {folder}/{fname} sweep {k}: amplitude {r.amp50[k]:.2f}, baseline {r.base[k]:.2f} {r.units}")
sat = sum(int((files.loc[i, "base"] <= -1999).sum()) for c in ["pre_rows", "post_rows"]
          for rows_ in inc[inc.has_data][c] for i in rows_)
print("Sweeps pinned at -2000 pA within the analysed pre- and post-pairing epochs (all kept):", sat)

The Concatenate*, *_PRE and *_POST files are copies of original recordings joined end to end: their sweeps are found in the originals one for one (all but 1 of 218 in VCB26, 80 of 215 in VCB21/Concatenate001, an excluded cell), so each recording is counted once and only the originals are used. Four of the copies (VCB12_POST, VCB13_PRE, VCB13_Post, VCB15_PRE) hold the same 10000 samples per sweep as the originals but their headers give 10 kHz and 1 s sweeps, half the true rate (a finding). One sweep is identical in three recordings of different days (VC2, VC3 and VCB19): it is pinned at -2000 pA, the amplifier's limit, with no response, so it is not a recording deposited twice. Within the analysed epochs such sweeps are counted above and kept, with an amplitude of 0, as the paper names no rule for dropping sweeps.

The descriptor puts the stimulus "typically around 100 ms into the recordings". The artifact's onset is at 107.80 or 107.85 ms in 16705 of 17319 test sweeps; within a file, 16351 sweeps near 108 ms share the file's most common onset, 354 are one sample (0.05 ms) away (120 before, 234 after) and 5 further. In seven files 26 to 89% of the sweeps have it at 87 to 99 ms and in three more 1 or 2% do, ten files in all, which is why it is found per sweep. IC13 and VCB19 also appear in the list of files with sweeps before 105 ms, but only through their sweeps with no stimulus (onset at 50 to 60 ms), which are dropped below. The artifact is biphasic and its largest step falls 0 to 0.2 ms after the onset, at different places in different sweeps of 41 of 115 files: aligning on the largest step, as the first version of this entry did, shifted sweeps by up to 0.2 ms against each other. Aligning on the onset removes this. Five sweeps hold no stimulus artifact and are dropped: four post-pairing sweeps of IC13 (one with no step, three whose largest step is a spike's upstroke, at 54 to 124 ms) and the VCB19 sweep pinned at -2000 pA. The artifact ends 0.55 to 2.55 ms after the onset (median 0.55), and no peak falls on the first sample of its window.

In every analysed cell but VCB17 the response after the stimulus is at least twice the same measure taken before it, and the group medians are 15 to 54 times, so the evoked responses are locked to the stimulus in each sweep (there are no trial tables; each sweep is one stimulus). # VCB17: its pre-pairing response, measured per sweep, is less than twice the same measure before the stimulus
# (above). Its median traces, holding current and amplitudes, pre and post.

z0, sr = 300, 20                      # median_trace starts 15 ms (300 samples) before the stimulus; 20 samples/ms
rows = []
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.2))
for name, key in [("pre", "pre_rows"), ("post", "post_rows")]:
    f = files.loc[c17[key][-1] if name == "pre" else c17[key][0]]
    tr = f.median_trace - f.median_trace[z0 - 10 * sr:z0].mean()
    end = int(round(f.artifact_end_ms * sr))
    seg = -tr[z0 + end:z0 + 50 * sr + 1]
    ep = {k: pvc9.epoch_amplitudes(files, c17[key], key=k) for k in ["amp50", "amp_prestim", "amp50_base50", "base"]}
    if name == "pre":                 # the analysed epoch: the last 120 baseline sweeps
        ep = {k: x[-pvc9.N_PRE:] for k, x in ep.items()}
    rows.append(dict(epoch=name, file=f.file, sweeps=len(ep["amp50"]),
                     median_trace_peak_pA=seg.max(), peak_ms=(end + seg.argmax()) / sr,
                     sweep_amp_median=np.median(ep["amp50"]), sweep_amp_mean=ep["amp50"].mean(),
                     prestim_reference_median=np.median(ep["amp_prestim"]),
                     amp_50ms_baseline_mean=ep["amp50_base50"].mean(),
                     holding_median_pA=np.median(ep["base"]), holding_sd_pA=np.std(ep["base"])))
    axes[0].plot(np.arange(len(tr)) / sr - 15, tr, lw=0.8, label=f"{name} (median of the file's {f.n_sweeps} sweeps)")
    axes[1].plot(ep["amp50"], ".", ms=3, label=name)
    axes[1].plot(ep["amp_prestim"], ".", ms=2, c="grey", label="before the stimulus" if name == "pre" else None)
    axes[2].plot(ep["base"], ".", ms=3, label=name)

The artifact runs beyond the first panel's axes; the other panels show every analysed sweep.

VCB17 has a stimulus-locked inward current before pairing: its median trace peaks at 93 pA, 3 ms after the stimulus, and the median of its per-sweep amplitudes (94.3 pA) is 1.9 times the same measure before the stimulus (median 49.5 pA), which is why it is listed above as below 2: the per-sweep peak carries some noise, and the response is shown by the median traces. After pairing the median trace peaks at 473 pA. The change is +408% from the median traces, +390% from the sweep means and +388% with a 50 ms baseline, so it does not depend on the baseline window. The holding current is steady over the analysed sweeps (median -486 and -484 pA). The sheet's amplitudes (-579 and -943 pA) less the holding current give -94 and -459 pA, a change of +390%, the value measured here: the sheet's +62.9% is computed on amplitudes that include the holding current. VCB17 is kept, as a cell the paper included whose response is measurable; its change is a large potentiation by every estimate.

The data set's own per-cell changes (Summary sheets, computed by the authors in Excel from Clampfit measurements) agree with this measure for most cells (34 of 46 within 5 points under (P)(c), and the pre-pairing amplitudes within a median 3.4%), which supports the measure and the epochs. The larger differences may come from the sweeps the authors selected (each sheet marks its sweeps in green) or, for VCB17, from an amplitude that includes the holding current (above). The sheet values are shown for comparison only; every result below is computed from the recordings.

IC13's sheet holds its per-sweep amplitudes: the 120 green values are the last 120 measured baseline sweeps (r = 0.998, mean difference -0.006 mV), and the 73 values after them are the first 73 post-pairing sweeps (r = 0.995, +0.023 mV). The post-pairing file has 77 sweeps; the last four hold no stimulus artifact (one has no step at all, three a spike, measured at 43 to 51 mV), and the sheet leaves them out. Measured with them, as in the first version of this entry, IC13 changed by +20.6%; without them it changes by -10.9%, against -12.8% in its sheet, and is NC in every reading.

# The alignment and the baseline: the per-cell change with the first version's alignment (each sweep on its
# largest step), with the 10 ms baseline ending 1 ms before the stimulus, and with a 50 ms baseline.
rows = []
for k in ["amp50_maxstep", "amp50_guard", "amp50_base50"]:
    m = res.merge(pvc9.classify_all(files, cells, key=k), on=["cell", "P", "T"], suffixes=("", "_v"))
    d = (m.change - m.change_v).abs()
    rows.append(dict(variant=k, median_abs_diff=d.median(), max_abs_diff=d.max(), cell_of_max=m.cell[d.idxmax()],
                     class_changes=int((m.cls != m.cls_v).sum()),
                     which=", ".join(sorted({f"{c} ({P},{T}) {a}->{b}" for c, P, T, a, b in
                                             zip(m.cell, m.P, m["T"], m.cls, m.cls_v) if a != b}))))
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3).to_string(index=False))

      variant  median_abs_diff  max_abs_diff cell_of_max  class_changes                                                                              which
amp50_maxstep            0.216        10.105       VCB17              4 VCB33 (a,a) LTD->NC, VCB33 (a,b) LTD->NC, VCB33 (b,a) LTD->NC, VCB33 (b,b) LTD->NC
  amp50_guard            0.020         0.257       VCB19              0                                                                                   
 amp50_base50            0.089         1.911       VCB17              2                                             IC16 (b,a) LTP->NC, IC16 (b,b) LTP->NC

Aligning on the largest step (the first version) moves the per-cell change by a median 0.22 points (at most 10 points, VCB17's +390%) and changes one cell's class: VCB33 is LTD after onset alignment and NC under readings (a) and (b) after largest-step alignment. Ending the 10 ms baseline 1 ms before the stimulus moves the change by a median 0.02 points (at most 0.26) and changes no class, so no artifact sample enters the baseline. A 50 ms baseline moves it by a median 0.09 points and changes IC16's class in reading (b), where its change is +15.1%, at the threshold.

Every analysed cell has at least 120 pre-pairing sweeps, and most have more (up to 400). Five have fewer than 120 post-pairing sweeps (73 to 119 measured); for them readings (P)(b) and (P)(c) use every post-pairing sweep, the same as (a). Post-pairing recordings start 9.8 to 12.4 min after the pairing begins, as 60 trials at 0.1 Hz require. Five IC cells had a second pairing; only the first and the recording before the second are used.

Which 120 baseline sweeps form the pre-pairing epoch is not fixed by the claims file. The Methods say pairing began "after the pre-pairing epoch was complete (120 stimuli at 0.2 Hz)", which reads as the 120 sweeps just before pairing, and the data set's own sheets agree: their mean pre-pairing amplitudes match the last 120 sweeps (median difference 4.5%) and not the first 120 (24.3%). The last 120 are used, as an assumption; the first 120 are run as a variant in each claim.

The post-pairing window (P) is a reading the claims file names. Where the readings of a claim of absence give different outcomes, the claims file has the author adopt one. This entry adopts (P)(c), the last 120 post-pairing sweeps: the Methods give "at least 10 more minutes of testing" after pairing, the 40 VC and VCB sheets that state it compared 120 traces ("Traces compared", 120), and of the two 120-sweep readings (c) is closer to the sheets' changes (34 of 46 cells within 5 points, median 2.0 points; (b) 30 of 46, 3.7 points).

Claims¶

Every per-cell result below comes from pvc9.classify_all, run once for each reading of (P) and (T). The control group is the 20 complete control recordings (10 IC, 10 VC); the bicuculline group is the 26 VCB recordings.

In [14]:
res = pvc9.classify_all(files, cells)
res_first = pvc9.classify_all(files, cells, pre_reading="first")      # variant: first 120 baseline sweeps
res_w30 = pvc9.classify_all(files, cells, window=30)                  # variant of (M): 30 ms window
res_var = {k: pvc9.classify_all(files, cells, key=k) for k in ["amp50_maxstep", "amp50_guard"]}   # alignment variants
res["control"] = res.group.isin(["IC", "VC"])
for r in (res_first, res_w30, *res_var.values()):
    r["control"] = r.group.isin(["IC", "VC"])

def counts(r, mask):
    out = r[mask].groupby(["P", "T"]).cls.value_counts().unstack(fill_value=0)
    for k in ["LTP", "LTD", "NC"]:
        if k not in out:
            out[k] = 0
    out = out[["LTP", "LTD", "NC"]]
    out["n"] = out.sum(axis=1)
    return out

print("Rows:", len(res), "=", res.cell.nunique(), "cells x 3 readings of (P) x 2 of (T)")

Rows: 276 = 46 cells x 3 readings of (P) x 2 of (T)

dataset-size¶

Plasticity was analysed in 28 control cells (14 in voltage clamp, 14 in current clamp) and 26 cells with 2 uM bicuculline in the bath.

Criterion: counts of the included cells, zero tolerance; the bicuculline cells are voltage clamp; 27 would be partially reproduced; the discarded recordings (9 IC, 11 VC, 12 bicuculline) are counted where the data set holds them.

Result: reproduced. The Summary sheets mark exactly 14 IC, 14 VC and 26 bicuculline recordings as included and 9, 11 and 12 as excluded, the paper's numbers, and every bicuculline test file is in voltage clamp (pA), as the Methods and Figure 2 say and the Dataset paragraph's "I-clamp" does not. The included rows are unfilled (IC, VCB) or green (VC), and every excluded row is red. The deposit holds complete recordings for all 26 bicuculline cells but for only 10 of the 14 IC and 10 of the 14 VC control cells; this limits the claims below, not the count of cells the paper analysed, which the sheets give with a row and per-sweep amplitudes for each.

fig1c-control-outcomes¶

With inhibition intact, few cells showed plasticity after pairing; 1 of 28 underwent LTP, 3 of 28 LTD and 24 of 28 no change.

Criterion: reproduced when, under one reading of (P) and (T), the counts are 1 LTP, 3 LTD, 24 NC; partially when LTP plus LTD number 2 to 6 and NC is within 2.4 of 24. Only 20 of the 28 cells have complete recordings. For seven of the other eight the Summary sheet lists a change below 15% in size, which makes them NC under the paper's rule whatever the t-test gives; IC23's -24.6% leaves it LTD or NC. The counts out of 28 are therefore given as the 20 measured cells plus 7 NC, with IC23 either way (a deviation: the classes of the eight are bounded from the data set's own sheet values, not measured).

Adding the seven missing cells that the sheets put below 15% as NC, the counts out of 28 meet the partial criterion (plastic 2 to 6, NC within 2.4 of 24) under (a,a), (a,b), (c,a) and (c,b) if IC23 is NC (3 LTP, 3 LTD, 22 NC under (a,a)), and under (c,b) if IC23 is LTD. This rests on the sheets as a bound for the missing cells, and the bound is not tight: of the 16 measured cells whose sheet change is below 15%, five (IC8, IC14, IC16, IC19, VC15) are plastic in some reading, two of them under (a,a). The sheets store no p values (the 14 VC sheets' "p (one-tail)" cells are empty, the IC sheets have none). The outcome also rests on the last 120 baseline sweeps: with the first 120, 8 to 11 of the 20 cells are plastic, mostly LTD.

fig1-control-no-net-plasticity¶

Over the 28 control cells, pairing gave no net plasticity of EPSPs or EPSCs.

Criterion: a claim of absence; a one-sample t-test of the per-cell percent changes against 0 at p < 0.05, in each reading of (P). Reproduced when no reading reaches p < 0.05.

fig1-vc-ic-same¶

Voltage-clamp and current-clamp control outcomes did not differ; both were Gaussian, and their means and variances did not differ, so the two were combined.

Criterion: claims of absence; Shapiro-Wilk on each group, a two-sample Student's t-test and a two-sided F-test of the variances, at p < 0.05, in each reading of (P). Reproduced when no reading has any test reach p < 0.05; not reproduced when every reading has one that does.

In [19]:
def ftest(x, y):
    """Two-sided F-test of the ratio of variances, var(x) / var(y)."""
    F = np.var(x, ddof=1) / np.var(y, ddof=1)
    p = 2 * min(stats.f.cdf(F, len(x) - 1, len(y) - 1), stats.f.sf(F, len(x) - 1, len(y) - 1))
    return F, min(p, 1.0)

rows = []
for P in "abc":
    r = res[res.control & (res.P == P) & (res["T"] == "a")]
    vc, ic = r[r.group == "VC"].change.values, r[r.group == "IC"].change.values
    F, pF = ftest(vc, ic)
    rows.append(dict(P=P, shapiro_vc=stats.shapiro(vc).pvalue, shapiro_ic=stats.shapiro(ic).pvalue,
                     t_p=stats.ttest_ind(vc, ic).pvalue, mean_diff=vc.mean() - ic.mean(), F=F, F_p=pF))
out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out["any_p_below_0.05"] = out[["shapiro_vc", "shapiro_ic", "t_p", "F_p"]].min(axis=1) < 0.05
print(out.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPaper: Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.79 (VC), 0.85 (IC); t-test p = 0.28; F-test p = 0.61.")
for P in "abc":
    r = res_first[res_first.control & (res_first.P == P) & (res_first["T"] == "a")]
    vc, ic = r[r.group == "VC"].change.values, r[r.group == "IC"].change.values
    print(f"Variant, first 120 baseline sweeps, ({P}): Shapiro VC p = {stats.shapiro(vc).pvalue:.3f}, IC p = {stats.shapiro(ic).pvalue:.3f}, "
          f"t p = {stats.ttest_ind(vc, ic).pvalue:.3f}, F p = {ftest(vc, ic)[1]:.3f}")

Readings (a,a) (8, 9, 9), (a,b) (7, 8, 11), (b,a) (8, 7, 11), (c,a) and (c,b) (7, 8, 11) have LTP and LTD each within 2 of the paper and both present; (b,b) has 6 LTD. Every reading has 14 to 17 plastic cells of 26, of both signs. The 30 ms window, the 1 ms baseline gap and the one-sided test give the same counts; largest-step alignment gives 8, 8, 10 under (a,a). The first 120 baseline sweeps give 6 LTP and 11 to 14 LTD, outside the partial criterion.

bicuculline-increases-plastic-fraction¶

Blocking GABAA inhibition raised the fraction of cells with plasticity from 4 of 28 to 16 of 26, showing that inhibition limits plasticity induction onto L4 cells.

Criterion: reproduced when, under the same reading for both groups, the bicuculline fraction of plastic cells is larger than the control fraction and both counts are within tolerance (4 +/- 0.4, 16 +/- 1.6); partially when the fraction is larger but a count is outside tolerance. Fisher's exact test as a variant. The control count is out of the 20 measured cells and, as in fig1c-control-outcomes, out of 28 with the eight missing cells bounded from their sheet values.

In [23]:
rows = []
for (P, T), r in c20.iterrows():
    pc = r.LTP + r.LTD
    rb = cb.loc[(P, T)]
    pb = rb.LTP + rb.LTD
    for ic23 in ["NC", "LTD"]:
        pc28 = pc + (ic23 == "LTD")
        odds, pf = stats.fisher_exact([[pb, 26 - pb], [pc28, 28 - pc28]])
        rows.append(dict(P=P, T=T, IC23=ic23, control_plastic=f"{pc}/20, {pc28}/28", control_frac=pc28 / 28,
                         bic_plastic=f"{pb}/26", bic_frac=pb / 26, larger=pb / 26 > pc28 / 28,
                         control_in_tol=abs(pc28 - 4) <= 0.4, bic_in_tol=abs(pb - 16) <= 1.6, fisher_p=pf))
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nOn the 20 measured control cells alone:")
for (P, T), r in c20.iterrows():
    pc, pb = r.LTP + r.LTD, cb.loc[(P, T)].LTP + cb.loc[(P, T)].LTD
    print(f"  ({P},{T}) control {pc}/20 = {pc / 20:.2f}, bicuculline {pb}/26 = {pb / 26:.2f}, "
          f"Fisher p = {stats.fisher_exact([[pb, 26 - pb], [pc, 20 - pc]])[1]:.4f}")

Result: partially reproduced, resting on assumptions. In every reading the plastic fraction is larger in bicuculline (14 to 17 of 26, 54 to 65%) than in control (5 to 7 of the 20 measured, 5 to 8 of 28 with the missing cells bounded). The bicuculline count is within 16 +/- 1.6 in every reading but (b,b) (14), but the control count is never within 4 +/- 0.4. Fisher's exact test gives p = 0.002 to 0.096 against the bounded 28 (p = 0.036 to 0.24 against the 20 measured).

fig2-subgroup-changes¶

In bicuculline, LTP cells changed by +39.9 +/- 14.7%, LTD cells by -38.5 +/- 20.4%, and NC cells by -3.0 +/- 7.6% on average.

Criterion: means over the cells of each class, under the same reading as fig2a-bicuculline-outcomes; tolerances 5.56, 6.8 and 2.4. Reproduced when all three are within tolerance under one reading; partially when two are.

In [24]:
rows = []
exp = {"LTP": (39.9, 5.56), "LTD": (-38.5, 6.8), "NC": (-3.0, 2.4)}
for (P, T), r in res[res.group == "VCB"].groupby(["P", "T"]):
    row = dict(P=P, T=T)
    k = 0
    for c, (v, tol) in exp.items():
        x = r[r.cls == c].change
        row[f"{c}_n"] = len(x)
        row[f"{c}_mean"] = x.mean()
        row[f"{c}_sd"] = x.std(ddof=1)
        ok = abs(x.mean() - v) <= tol if len(x) else False
        row[f"{c}_ok"] = ok
        k += ok
    row["within"] = k
    rows.append(row)
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(2).to_string(index=False))

The LTP mean is raised by VCB17, whose EPSC grows by about +390% (the data check shows this is a real response, and that the sheet's +63% includes the holding current). Without it the LTP mean is +33.4 to +37.1%, within tolerance under (a,b), (b,a) and (b,b).

fig2-mean-unchanged-variance-increased¶

The mean change over all cells did not differ between bicuculline (-3.8 +/- 34.3%) and control (-3.5 +/- 10.3%), but the variance of plasticity outcomes was significantly larger in bicuculline.

Criterion: two-sample Student's t-test of the means, judged as absence in each reading of (P); a two-sided F-test of the variances with p < 0.01 and the bicuculline variance larger, in the same reading; the bicuculline mean (-3.8 +/- 6.73) and SD (34.3 +/- 3.43) within tolerance. Reproduced when all hold; partially when the two tests hold but a value is outside tolerance.

    F, pF = ftest(b, c)
    rows.append(dict(P=P, n_bic=len(b), bic_mean=b.mean(), bic_sd=b.std(ddof=1), n_ctl=len(c), ctl_mean=c.mean(),
                     ctl_sd=c.std(ddof=1), t_p=stats.ttest_ind(b, c).pvalue, F=F, F_p=pF,

fig3a-ks-scs-vs-ecs, fig3c-random-mixing-narrower, fig3b-segregation-near-complete¶

These three claims need the single-cell stimulation (SCS) data of the paper's reference 17 (per-connection strengths before and after pairing, n = 42 or 43). The data set does not hold them (the archive's listing above has only the three ECS folders and their sheets), the paper gives no location, and no CRCNS data set of these authors holds them (the bucket's pvc-1 to pvc-13 were listed while preparing this entry; only pvc-9 is theirs). They are blocked as data_missing.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The paper measured amplitudes in Clampfit, on sweeps it selected, and gives no peak window, baseline, post-pairing window or form of t-test. Here the claims file's measure is used on every sweep that holds a stimulus artifact, with each sweep aligned on the artifact's onset and the end of the artifact found per file; the post-pairing window and the t-test are run under every reading. The pre-pairing epoch is the last 120 baseline sweeps, an assumption supported by the Methods' wording and by the data set's own sheets; the first 120 change several outcomes and are shown as a variant. Where readings of the post-pairing window disagree on a claim of absence, the last 120 sweeps are adopted. Cells with two pairings use the first. The control group is 20 of the paper's 28 cells, as 8 have no complete recording.

What was found about the data set.

  • Eight of the 28 included control recordings are missing or incomplete: IC22, IC23, VC21 and VC25 have no folder; VC10 and VC17 have no post-pairing recording; IC11's post-pairing recording is not in its folder (its sheet names the pairing file as the post-pairing one); IC7's listed post-pairing file (07305017) has no protocol, no date and no evoked response at the usual time.
  • Folder IC6 is empty and the IC6 recording is in folder IC7, with IC7's own.
  • The descriptor says sweeps are "triggered once every 10 seconds"; test sweeps are every 5 s (0.2 Hz), as the Methods say; only pairing trials are every 10 s.
  • The derived files (Concatenate*, *_PRE, *_POST) duplicate the original recordings; four give half the true sampling rate in their headers. The archive also holds .sta, .tmp and .bak files that the descriptor does not mention.
  • The stimulus falls 9 to 20 ms earlier in some sweeps of 10 files.
  • The sheets store no p values (the VC sheets' "p (one-tail)" cells are empty).
  • The Summary sheets' per-cell changes reproduce the paper's bicuculline mean and SD (-3.76 +/- 34.25%), but their IC and VC values (-5.79 +/- 9.51%, -3.14 +/- 13.40%) do not match the paper's I-clamp and V-clamp values (-1.41 +/- 10.92%, -5.67 +/- 9.47%); the IC values are close to the paper's V-clamp ones.
  • For VCB17 the sheet's amplitudes include the holding current: less the holding current they give the +390% change measured here, not the sheet's +62.9%, which enters the bicuculline mean and SD that the sheets share with the paper.
